$comment: Declarative corpus spec. `collect.js` reads this, walks each root recursively, and,selects deterministically (sort by relative path, take the first `limit`).,,Roots are machine-specific by nature — this corpus is third-party source found on a,developer machine, not vendored bytes. That is deliberate: vendoring GPL/BSD source into,this repo to measure a classifier would be a licensing problem for a measurement.,The recipe is the reproducible artifact; `manifest.json` records what a given machine,actually produced, so two runs on the same machine are comparable and a run on a,different machine is visibly a different corpus rather than silently one.,,`expect` is asserted after selection. It exists because the 4b.3 A/B loop globbed one,directory level and measured 132 of 144 files without noticing (see,docs/phase-4b-lever-disposition.md finding 3). A count that is not asserted is a count,that will be wrong eventually. | 2026-08-09: typescript 56->57->59 and prose 25->28. These buckets count this repository's own files, which grow; the harness refusing on the mismatch is it working. The 57->59 step is src/cli/ingest.ts and src/core/render/index.ts, added by audit H5. | 2026-08-10: typescript 59->60 and prose 28->29, during audit Wave 2. The typescript file is src/bench/fixtures/bundled-path.ts (audit M10); the prose file is docs/audit-remediation-status.md, which landed in 7a1b5a7 AFTER the dd540fe baseline was recorded, so that one was already outstanding. Both denominators moved, so Wave 2 aggregates are NOT directly comparable to the dd540fe table - compare per-file rows over the shared set instead. | 2026-08-10, audit decisions H2/M1/M11: typescript 60->61 (src/core/validation/language-support.ts, H2) and prose 29->18 (M11 retired twelve narrative documents and added docs/retired-documents.md). The prose bucket is now 18 real documents rather than 29 — a smaller negative set for looksLikeMarkdown, and deliberately so: what it lost was superseded phase narrative, not a different kind of prose. | 2026-08-11, targetReductionRatio made real: typescript 61->62 (src/core/budget/index.ts). NOTE the corpus is measured at ratio 0.3 and this change makes that ratio BIND, so aggregates move by design: python file 23.14%->20.26% and typescript file 23.03%->17.57%, while fallbacks FELL (python 14->13) and reduced counts ROSE. Lower aggregate here is the target being honoured, not a regression - compare per-file adherence, not the mean. | 2026-08-20, widening elision to Go (step 1 of DECISIONS 56): prose 18->17. Nothing was removed - DECISIONS.md crossed maxBytes as it grew (222,371 bytes against the 204,800 cap), so the walk still SEES 18 files and only 17 are eligible. The cap is deliberately NOT raised: raising it would change what the prose bucket measures and move every prose aggregate, in order to keep one file whose growth is the reason it no longer fits. Prose aggregates from here are over 17 documents and are not comparable to earlier 18-document ones; per-row over one frozen corpus still is. | 2026-09-19, R2 latency baseline: typescript 62->63 and prose 17->21. The typescript file is src/core/validation/ast/go-validator.ts (DECISIONS 60), which landed in v1.6.1 on 2026-08-30 - the recipe was updated after step 1 of the Go work and not after step 2, so this count was stale for three weeks and five PRs. The prose files are docs/security-review-2026-08-30.md, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-09-tokendamper-v2-roadmap-design.md, oxaudit.md and oxaudit-split.md. NOTHING here was added by the work being measured - the drift is entirely pre-existing and surfaced only because R2 is the first corpus run since v1.6.1, which is the cost of landing five doc-and-security PRs that were correctly off the optimize route. Reduction aggregates from here are over 63 typescript and 21 prose files and are NOT comparable to earlier ones. The latency baseline recorded alongside this has no predecessor, so it is unaffected by the change. | 2026-09-19, R3 start: prose 21->22. The file is docs/r3-start-here.md, the R3 handoff, added by commit f06fd30 AFTER the R2 latency baseline was frozen at fcb6718 — so the drift is the handoff document counting itself, not the work being measured. NOTE this one is expected to reverse: docs/r3-start-here.md is written to be DELETED when R3 lands, at which point the walk sees 21 again and the harness refuses in the other direction. Update expect back to 21 in the same commit that removes the file. Prose aggregates from here are over 22 documents and are not comparable to the 21-document R2 baseline; per-row over one frozen corpus still is. | 2026-09-23, R3 step 3: `.superpowers` added to excludeDirs, and the typescript limit raised 64->80. The exclusion is the `.agents` lesson repeating: `.superpowers/sdd/` holds this workflow's own briefs, reports and ledger, and because sort-then-take is alphabetical they took 19 of the 40 prose slots and pushed out real documents (prose eligible read 41 against an expected 22). The limit raise is different in kind: src grew to 67 eligible files, so for the first time in this corpus's history the typescript limit BOUND, silently dropping 3 files rather than refusing. Every earlier entry here moved `expect` while `limit` stayed slack; raising it keeps the bucket meaning what its `why` says - the repo's own source - instead of the first 64 paths alphabetically. The typescript expect moves 63->67 in the same change: src gained src/core/parser/coverage.ts, src/core/parser/mode.ts and src/cli/deep-backends.ts from R3 step 3 itself, plus one pre-existing file that crossed minBytes. Note src/core/parser/mode.ts is 913 bytes and therefore NOT eligible - the arithmetic only works if you check sizes rather than counting new files. Reduction aggregates from here are over 67 typescript files and are NOT comparable to the 63-file R2/R3-step-1 baselines; per-row over one frozen corpus still is. | 2026-09-23, R3 lands: prose 22->21. docs/r3-start-here.md is deleted, which is the reversal its own 2026-09-19 entry predicted and asked for in the same commit that removes the file. | 2026-09-23, R4 handoff: prose 21->22. The file is docs/r4-start-here.md, the R4 pointer document, and like docs/r3-start-here.md before it the drift is the handoff counting itself rather than the work being measured. Expected to reverse: set expect back to 21 in the same commit that deletes the file when R4 lands. | 2026-10-04, R4 design: prose 22->23. The file is docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-04-r4-c-csharp-and-v2-release-design.md, the approved design for R4 and v2.0.0; the drift is the design counting itself, not the work being measured. Unlike the start-here pointers it is NOT deleted when R4 lands, so when docs/r4-start-here.md goes the count falls by one from whatever it is then, not to 21. | 2026-10-04, R4 plan: prose 23->24. The file is docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-04-r4-c-csharp-and-v2-release.md, the implementation plan for the design above; like the design it stays when R4 lands. | 2026-10-04, R4 step 1: typescript 67->69. The files are src/core/validation/ast/c-validator.ts and src/core/validation/ast/csharp-validator.ts, the C and C# lexers (DECISIONS 84) - the work being measured adding its own source to the corpus that measures it, which is why every R4 A/B is per-row over one frozen corpus rather than a comparison of aggregates. | 2026-10-05, R4 lands: typescript 69->70, prose stays 24. docs/r4-start-here.md is deleted, the reversal its own 2026-09-23 entry asked for in the same commit that removes the file; packages/deep/README.md, the published package's README from R4 Part B, takes its place in the count. The typescript file is src/core/parser/deep-only.ts from R4 step 2 (DECISIONS 85), which did not update this recipe - the stale-count pattern of 2026-09-19 again, caught by the next full collect. The R4 design and plan stay, as their entries said they would.
